text: OVERDOSAGE The symptoms of overdosage of glycopyrrolate are peripheral in nature rather than central. 1. To guard against further absorption of the drug-use gastric lavage, cathartics and/or enemas. 2. To combat peripheral anticholinergic effects (residual mydriasis, dry mouth, etc.)-utilize a quaternary ammonium anticholinesterase, such as neostigmine methylsulfate. 3. To combat hypotension-use pressor amines (norepinephrine, metaraminol) i.v.; and supportive care. 4. To combat respiratory depression-administer oxygen; utilize a respiratory stimulant such as Dopram ®* i.v.; artificial respiration.
